question.text: Mohini Capital Category I SSF (Special Situation Fund) wants to invest in Security Receipts (SRs) issued by an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC). Per Chapter 9, which restriction applies?

answer.text: No restrictions; any AIF can buy any ARC SR.
AIFs can buy SRs of ANY ARC without conflict-check.

AIFs CANNOT invest in SRs (a) issued by an ARC which is the AIF's portfolio investee company, or (b) where the SR becomes a related-party transaction (backed by underlying loans of the AIF's associate / group companies).
Only Cat III AIFs are permitted to invest in ARC SRs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 lists two specific restrictions on AIF investments in ARC SRs: (a) an AIF cannot invest in SRs issued by an ARC which is its portfolio investee company, and (b) an AIF cannot invest in SRs that would become related-party transactions (backed by the underlying loans of its associate or group companies) because of the potential conflict of interest. Option C captures both restrictions. The Trap: Options A and B ignore the conflict-of-interest carve-outs by allowing any AIF to buy any ARC SR. Option D wrongly restricts SR access to Category III AIFs, whereas the workbook places Category II AIFs squarely within the eligible investor universe for ARC SRs subject to the stated restrictions. Note: SSF is a sub-category under Category I AIF, while Category II AIFs are categorised as QIBs under the SARFAESI Act for the purpose of investing in ARC SRs. The two restrictions in Option C apply to the AIF's SR investments regardless of which sub-category vehicle is making the investment.
